h: DG goes full contrarian while Forbes and Saliba ride the chalk
b: DG is fading the sportsbook favorite in 8 of 14 games, opening with EDM (+150) and CHI (+136). If the dogs bark, he cashes the fattest shares on the board. Forbes and Saliba agree on 11 of 14, so they're mostly splitting the same pots. All four are on FLA, MTL and MIN, so nothing moves there. Matchup to watch: LAK @ OTT, where DG is alone on the Kings.

h: Saliba flips to the dogs as JB and Cory join the pool
b: Saliba ditched the chalk and now has 6 underdogs, including a lone-wolf VAN (+230) against four MIN backers at -285. If Vancouver pulls the upset, he pockets all 5 points in that game. Cory is all-in on 14 picks with 5 dogs, while JB has only 4 picks in so far, leaving 10 games on the table. The opener, EDM @ CAR, is now a 3-3 split worth 2 points a head either way.

h: Cam enters chalky as three games split dead even
b: Cam joined with all 14 picks and just 2 underdogs, piling onto the favorites. That leaves CBJ-TOR, VGK-WPG and SEA-SJS as perfect 3-3 splits, worth 2 points a head no matter who wins. The biggest lottery ticket on the board: Saliba is alone on PHI (+140) against six MTL backers, so a Flyers win hands him all 7 points.

h: Late flips: Forbes joins DG on the Kings, Saliba on the Blues
b: Forbes switched LAK @ OTT to the Kings (+145), and Saliba moved to STL (+110) against the Devils. Both games are now 2-4 splits, so if either underdog wins, its two backers take 3 points apiece. DG is on both of those dogs, giving him the biggest swing in the two games.

h: Game day: Saliba opens as the pool favorite at +143
b: With the first puck at 10am PT, Saliba carries a 41% chance to win, driven by lone-wolf tickets on VAN and PHI. DG is next at 24% (+309) as the field's biggest contrarian. Line watch: CAR stretched to -198 over EDM, and DET slid to +102 against the Islanders with five of seven players on Detroit. JB is still sitting on 4 picks, with until each puck drop to fill in the rest.

h: 10 deep at puck drop: Saliba the +134 favorite, Mark the new No. 2
b: The field grew to 10 with Mark, Hutson and Adam joining, and JB finally filled all 14 picks. Saliba opens at 43% to take the pot (+134), with newcomer Mark next at 13% (+692). The 10am opener, EDM @ CAR, splits 6-4 for Carolina at -218: a Hurricanes win pays 1.7 a head, but if the Oilers pull it off, DG, Mike, JB and Mark split 10 points for 2.5 each.

h: Mazu crashes Saliba's party as the opener gets underway
b: Late entry Mazu matched Saliba on both of his lone-wolf longshots, PHI and VAN, cutting Saliba's title odds from 43% to 24% (+320). Saliba is still the favorite, with Mike (+691) and Mazu (+717) next among 11 players. EDM @ CAR is scoreless early in the 1st, with seven on Carolina (-238) and four on Edmonton (+195).

h: Canes storm back: CAR leads EDM 6-4 late in the 3rd
b: Carolina erased a 3-1 hole and leads 6-4 with 8 minutes left, a 98% win chance per the model. If it holds, the seven CAR backers split 11 points for 1.6 apiece, and the Oilers crew (DG, Mike, JB, Mark) gets shut out. Saliba remains the pool favorite at +245 (29%), with Mazu next at +595. CHI @ CGY just dropped the puck, and the 4pm slate's early pair, BUF @ FLA and PIT @ NSH, are both 5-6 splits.

h: DG's late flip to the Oilers backfires as seven Canes backers cash
b: DG started on Carolina, jumped to Edmonton, and watched the Canes win 7-4. That flip cost him 1.6 points, and it drops him to last in win odds at +1778. Mike, JB and Mark rode the Oilers down with him, while seven Carolina backers bank 1.6 each. Saliba stays the favorite at +294, but his seven switches, nearly all to the underdog, still need the dogs to start barking.

h: Saliba's switch to the Hawks is sweating as Calgary strikes first
b: Saliba flipped CHI @ CGY from Calgary to Chicago, and the Flames lead 1-0 in the 1st. DG and Mike are on the Hawks with him, so the crew burned by the Oilers needs a comeback: a Chicago win splits 11 points three ways for 3.7 each. The eight Calgary backers would get 1.4 apiece.

h: Saliba's Hawks switch cashes big; Forbes flipped the wrong way
b: Saliba swapped Calgary for Chicago, the Hawks rallied to win 4-3, and he banked 3.7 points to lead with 5.2 and a 48% shot at the pot (+110). Forbes made the opposite move, ditching Chicago for Calgary, and gets nothing. Saliba and DG also both switched to Pittsburgh, who lead Nashville 2-1. Last call: the seven-game 4pm slate locks at puck drop.

h: Saliba nears even money as his switch to the Blues jumps out 2-0
b: Saliba's flip from the Devils to the Blues is paying early, with St. Louis up 2-0, and he's now a coin flip to take the pot at +103 (49%). Mike (+526) and DG (+635) are the main chasers at 3.7 points each. Mazu keeps riding Saliba's coattails, matching him on BUF, PIT, PHI, LAK, NYI and STL, but sits way back at +1481.

h: Mike leads on points, but Saliba is now a -207 favorite
b: Mike is on fire with 3 straight wins and tops the board at 7.3 points, yet sits at just 5% to win. Saliba's switches to BUF and PIT both lost, but his lone-wolf-style plays on PHI (up 3-1) and STL (up 8-4) have him at 68% to take the pot. Hutson is the big mover at +525, while Cam, Cory and JB are down to 0% in the simulations.

h: Three-man race: Saliba and Mazu tied at 15.4, Adam lurking
b: Eleven games are final and the sims have cut the field to three. Saliba (48% to win) and Mazu (3 straight correct, 24%) are tied at 15.4 pts, and they're the only two on +260 Vancouver, so an upset there pays them 5.5 each. Adam sits 1.2 back at 14.2 with a 28% shot and needs Minnesota to hold. Forbes, Mike and the rest of the room are now just rooting for chaos.

h: Adam flips the board: now the +160 favorite with 3 games left
b: Adam is 1.2 pts back at 14.2 but the sims make him the favorite at 38%, because his path is simple: Utah, Minnesota and San Jose all win and he takes the pot. Saliba (+225) and Mazu (+224) are tied at 15.4 and both have Anaheim and +260 Vancouver, so they split those and Seattle-San Jose decides it between them. A Canucks upset or an Anaheim comeback knocks Adam out, and everyone else is already eliminated.

h: Overtime in Vancouver decides it: Adam or Mazu
b: Utah held on 3-2, so Adam takes the lead at 16.1 pts (56%), with Mazu and Saliba at 15.4. Minnesota and Vancouver are tied 3-3 after regulation: if the Wild win, Adam takes the pot, and if the Canucks win, Mazu does. Saliba (4%) needs Seattle to come back from 4-3 down with 2:01 left, and if they do, he wins no matter what happens in Vancouver.
